title: Search invariant
statement:
For a natural number $n$ and a Boolean list $S$, the search invariant holds exactly when there are natural numbers $c,d$ and a Boolean $b$ such that $S$ is the pair encoding of the binary expansion of $c$ and the pair encoding of the binary expansion of $d$ with the one-element list containing $b$, and
$2^{\lceil\log_2(2n)\rceil}<c\leq \operatorname{lovaszPrime}(n)$, $2\leq d\leq c$, no natural number $m$ with $2\leq m<d$ divides $c$, and $b=\mathrm{true}$ implies $c=\operatorname{lovaszPrime}(n)$.
caveat: The supplied material does not define the pair encoding or the function $\operatorname{lovaszPrime}$, so these constructions must retain their stated names.
